## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Make `--exclude` honor its required environment default so CI jobs can skip matching files without passing the flag explicitly.

## Changes

The pull request adds and documents a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that matches file names and logs skipped files in verbose mode. It adds tests for argument parsing, file selection, and archive contents.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` argument, the parser returns an empty list. The CLI policy says “Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable” (`.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`). — CI jobs that rely on `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` archive files they configured the tool to skip.

## Suggestions

- cli/main.py:33 — tests — Test exact-name exclusions in nested directories — The tests never check that `--exclude skip.log` excludes `sub/skip.log`. All matching cases use extension wildcards, which `fnmatch` also matches against full paths. — A regression to full-path matching would pass the suite while retaining nested files that users excluded by name.
